clue.text: 1000 1000 1000 — regular telnet, say

parts.note: split as 100 and 0: 100 is the Roman numeral C and 0 looks like the letter O
a thousand is M in Roman numerals
a thousand is M in Roman numerals again

indicators.note: regular means taking every other letter of the word telnet, here the even ones

explanation.surface: A string of numbers followed by a computing term, like a line of code or a terse network log.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 1000 is read as 100 then 0, giving C and O; the other two are plain Roman M. 'regular' takes the alternate letters E, N, T from telnet.
explanation.definitionFit: To remark on something is to say it, a straightforward verb synonym.

clue.text: Fraud takes skill to make a packet

indicators.note: takes means holds within, so the fraud goes round the skill

parts.note: a con is a swindle, a fraud
art means skill, as in the art of persuasion

explanation.surface: A swindler uses cunning to make a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'packet' looks like money in the surface (making a packet); it is a box.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardboard box for goods such as milk or cigarettes is a packet.

clue.text: Pick up a stumping, then English runs follow Moeen's debut

indicators.note: then says the next letters follow straight after
debut means first appearance, so the first letter of Moeen's

parts.note: st is the scorecard abbreviation for stumped in cricket
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A cricket commentary: catch, stumping and runs follow Moeen Ali's first game.
explanation.walkthrough: Moeen Ali is an England cricketer; 'follow' just orders the pieces after his initial.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick up a skill is to learn it until expert, the verb sense of mastering.

clue.text: Medicine pill initially consumed by some poorly sailors

indicators.note: being consumed by something means going inside it
poorly means unwell, out of sorts, so these letters are rearranged
initially points to the first letter of pill

parts.note: salts are old sailors, as in old salts

explanation.surface: Sick seamen are given medicine, starting with a pill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poorly' turns SOME into ESOM, which takes in P, the initial of pill.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnesium sulphate crystals taken as a laxative are a traditional remedy, a kind of medicine.

clue.text: Spike's t-trumpet

parts.note: a horn is a brass instrument like a trumpet

explanation.surface: Someone named Spike stutters while playing the trumpet.
explanation.walkthrough: The stammered t gives T before HORN.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp pointed growth on a stem is a spike or prickle.

clue.text: Grow striking moobs when ingesting powerful drugs, ultimately

indicators.note: striking in the sense of hitting hard, knocking these letters into a new order
ingesting means taking in, so the closing letters are absorbed among the chest letters before they are rearranged
ultimately points to the final letter of each of the words powerful and drugs

explanation.surface: A bodybuilder on steroids grows an impressive chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives L and S, the last letters of powerful and drugs, which join MOOBS; 'striking' rearranges the seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To flourish or develop is to grow, a verb synonym; a plant comes into flower as it thrives.

clue.text: Guard busy person with something light, not hard

parts.note: someone busy is said to be as busy as a bee

indicators.note: not says one letter is removed from the light thing

parts.note: a feather is the proverbially light thing
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A security guard is a busy worker, not given anything tough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not hard' takes H out of FEATHER to leave FEATER. A Beefeater is a Yeoman Warder at the Tower of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeoman Warders guarding the Tower of London are known by this nickname, so one is a guard.

clue.text: Work with metal and stone

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium, a metal

explanation.surface: A jeweller works with metal and gemstones.
explanation.definitionFit: A milky iridescent gem is a precious stone.

clue.text: More delicate girls go crazy over The Kinks

indicators.note: going crazy means going wild, so these letters run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: Delicate girls scream over the band The Kinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go crazy' rearranges GIRLS with THE; 'over' and 'Kinks' are surface dressing, Kinks hinting at twisting the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of slight, meaning more slender or frail, hence more delicate.

clue.text: Functioning swimming pool in my exclusive control

indicators.note: in says the earlier pieces sit inside the word my

parts.note: a machine that is on is functioning

indicators.note: swimming means floating about, so these letters drift into a new order

explanation.surface: A rich person boasts of a working pool all to themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the functioning word and the jumbled pool inside MY; 'swimming' is the anagram signal, not a description of the pool.
explanation.definitionFit: Sole command of a market or supply is a monopoly, exclusive control of it.

clue.text: Chances, as king's knight retreats in the opening

indicators.note: says the reversed knight sits at the start, ahead of the king's letters
retreating means going backwards, so the knight's title reads in reverse

parts.note: a knight is addressed as Sir
K is the chess abbreviation for king, with S from the possessive

explanation.surface: A chess player gambles by pulling the king's knight back during the opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening' looks like the chess opening; with 'in the' it says the backwards knight goes first. 'retreats' is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking risks means taking chances; both nouns name gambles on an uncertain outcome.

clue.text: Campaign speech concerns exercise

indicators.note: concerns read as surrounds, the speech wrapping around the exercise

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech
PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: A politician's campaign address is about fitness.
explanation.definitionFit: A military campaign is a planned operation, a near synonym in the sense of an organised action.

clue.text: Ready for new ideas, I depend on swing to take maiden

indicators.note: taking something in means holding it inside, so the maiden goes within the rearranged letters
to swing is to sway about, so these letters are moved into a new order

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: Someone liberal says they rely on swinging to win a girl over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swing' rearranges I DEPEND ON into OPENINDED, and 'to take' puts M inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being receptive to fresh thinking is what having an unprejudiced, tolerant mind means.

clue.text: Deliver joint on Sunday

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means coming after, so the joint follows the day

parts.note: the hip is a joint of the body

explanation.surface: A courier sends out a roast joint for Sunday lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' looks like the Sunday roast; it is the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: To send goods by post or carrier is a common sense of the verb, a synonym for delivering.

clue.text: When comedian Sue is alone, get up and start baking pastries

indicators.note: get up in a down clue means read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: Mel and Sue are a British comic double act, so Sue alone has no Mel

indicators.note: baking transforms ingredients, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Sue Perkins, hosting Bake Off without her partner, gets everyone baking pastries.
explanation.walkthrough: Mel Giedroyc and Sue Perkins, a British comedy duo, hosted The Great British Bake Off. NO MEL turned up by 'get up' gives LEMON, and 'baking' rearranges START.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemon tarts are individual sweet pastries filled with lemon curd.

clue.text: Scottish heaven and hell? A lot confused about England's crown

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the single letter, enclosing it
confused means muddled, so these letters are jumbled
the crown is the top, so the first letter of England's

explanation.surface: A query about whether heaven and hell are muddled up in the matter of the English monarchy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' jumbles AND HELL A LOT, and 'about' wraps those letters round E, the crown of England's. Land o' the Leal is a Scots phrase from a Lady Nairne song.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally the land of the faithful, an old Scots expression for paradise.

clue.text: Qualification on the boundaries of clarity and tact

parts.note: a diploma is a qualification

indicators.note: the boundaries of clarity are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A qualification in clear thinking and tact.
explanation.definitionFit: Skill in handling people sensitively is tact, a synonym in its everyday rather than political sense.

clue.text: Surprise is hard when following Villa

indicators.note: says the other pieces come after the football club's first name

parts.note: Aston Villa is a football club in Birmingham
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A football pundit is surprised how tough life is for Villa fans.
explanation.walkthrough: Aston Villa is an English football club, so Villa gives ASTON.
explanation.definitionFit: To astonish is to amaze, a stronger synonym for surprise as a verb.

clue.text: Rain leads to ruin

definitions.meaning: a heavy fall of rain or snow
a collapse or fall from power

explanation.surface: Bad weather brings disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a heavy shower of rain and the collapse of a person or regime.

clue.text: Small drinks for each offspring of athlete

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
ports are fortified wines
per means for each, as in per head
a son is a child, an offspring

explanation.surface: Small glasses are bought for each of a sports star's children.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyone who competes in athletics or other games is an athlete in the wide sense.

clue.text: Barista's first latte order causes row

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of Barista's
to order is to arrange, so the letters of latte are rearranged

explanation.surface: A barista's first latte order leads to an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' looks like a coffee order; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A row, rhyming with cow, is a quarrel, and a fight is a battle.

clue.text: Not sea? So ___

parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank: if it is not sea, then the gap is completed by saying it is dry ground

explanation.surface: A child's question about the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as IS LAND to complete 'Not sea? So is land'; the whole word means a piece of ground surrounded by sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The completed phrase reads as a sentence, and the whole word names a tract of ground ringed by water.

clue.text: Why a printer won't print noise?

definitions.text: Why a printer won't print noise?

parts.words: Why a printer won't print noise?
parts.note: a printer with nothing, zero, in the way of ink cannot print; that phrase is also the grunt of a pig

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about a faulty printer, perhaps expecting a mechanical noise.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a riddle: the printer has O (zero) ink, which split differently is a farmyard noise.
explanation.definitionFit: The grunt a pig makes is its characteristic noise, and zero ink explains the failed printing.

clue.text: They catch MPs sat squabbling over euro problem

indicators.note: squabbling MPs are in disarray, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Parliamentarians bicker over the trouble with the euro.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squabbling' rearranges MPS SAT with EURO; 'over' and 'problem' only join the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Spring traps for rodents are devices made to catch them, so the definition describes their function.

clue.text: Fashion line inside — it's painful on the eye

indicators.note: inside says the line goes within the other piece

parts.note: a stye is a painful swelling on the eyelid

explanation.surface: A fashion line that is an eyesore.
explanation.definitionFit: Fashion and style are synonyms for the current mode of dress.

clue.text: Time for a lark, perhaps

definitions.meaning: slang for a prison sentence, as in doing time
a lark is one example of a feathered creature

explanation.surface: Time for a bit of fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lark' looks like fun; it is the songbird. Bird, from rhyming slang bird-lime for time, is British slang for a prison term.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a prison sentence, and the class to which the lark belongs.

clue.text: First girl to swallow gallon in one? Fabulous!

parts.note: first is number one, the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: swallowing means taking in, so the girl's name goes round the other letters

parts.note: Mary is a girl's name
A is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: A first girlfriend downs a whole gallon at once, to cheers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' gives I as the number one; 'to swallow' puts the gallon, in and one inside the girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabulous in its root sense means belonging to fable, so made up or unreal.

clue.text: Democrat hailed some carriage

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A Democratic politician is cheered from a horse-drawn vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratha is a chariot or carriage in Indian tradition, used in temple processions.

clue.text: Jazz singer's festival

definitions.meaning: Billie, the jazz singer, had this surname; the possessive is the clue's link to the second sense
a festival is a day of celebration, a holy day

explanation.surface: A jazz vocalist's music festival.
explanation.definitionFit: Billie the jazz vocalist bore this surname, and a festival is a day off, originally a holy day.

clue.text: Meal project forgets starters in London

indicators.note: forgets starters means dropping the opening letter of each of the two words

parts.note: a feast is a lavish meal
to project something is to send it out

explanation.surface: A dinner scheme goes wrong when the organisers leave out the starters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forgets starters' drops the first letters of FEAST and SEND. The East End is a district of east London.
explanation.definitionFit: The area of London east of the City, historically working-class, is named by this phrase.
